stories.title: A Nobel laureate's committee affirms OpenAI's AI-made proof of half a Millennium Prize Problem
stories.summary: Experts appointed by OpenAI and led by physicist David Gross say they have verified its AI-generated proof of the existence of quantum Yang-Mills theory, checked in Lean. The 'mass gap' half remains unsolved, and they wrote: 'We do not claim to fully understand the proof yet.'

predictions.note: An AI-generated proof of the first part of the Yang-Mills Millennium Prize Problem was affirmed by an expert committee, a sign of AI speeding up hard science.

stories.title: Bessent: the Trump-Xi meeting will advance a new US-China dialogue on superintelligence
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Shenzhen meeting on the sidelines of the 18-19 Nov APEC summit will advance a bilateral dialogue on superintelligence, including best practices for testing advanced models before release and 'keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology', according to Reuters.

predictions.note: The US says next week's Trump-Xi meeting will advance a US-China dialogue on superintelligence risk, a step short of negotiations on slowing or auditing it.

stories.title: OpenAI's Control Room can stop a research-model job within 35 seconds
stories.summary: OpenAI described Control Room, a central system that tracks model workloads across its research infrastructure; it says the most time it takes to stop a job is 35 seconds, and if Control Room itself goes down, all inference requests are denied.

predictions.note: OpenAI built a fail-closed system to stop research-model jobs after earlier rogue-agent incidents; a voluntary, single-company control, not a mandate.

stories.title: Google staff are reportedly testing a fast new Gemini model code-named Hydrogen
stories.summary: According to Business Insider, Google gave staff access to a model known internally as Hydrogen, which an engineer described as 'very capable, fast and efficient'. Google declined to comment.

stories.title: Anthropic's bankers reportedly weigh a $1.5 trillion-plus IPO valuation
stories.summary: The Financial Times reported that Anthropic's bankers are preparing to raise its IPO valuation to $1.5 trillion or more, above the $70 to $78 a share range filed on Tuesday, and Bloomberg reported the IPO is said to be multiple times oversubscribed.

predictions.note: Bankers are reportedly weighing a $1.5 trillion-plus valuation for Anthropic's IPO; reported, and the shares have not been priced yet.

stories.title: OpenAI reportedly made $10 billion in a quarter and lost $10.9 billion
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that OpenAI's third-quarter revenue rose nearly 50% to about $10 billion, while its adjusted operating loss reached $10.9 billion.

stories.title: CoreWeave jumps more than 20% after its results, sparking an AI cloud rally
stories.summary: CoreWeave shares jumped more than 20% on Wednesday, igniting a rally in battered AI cloud stocks, as its heavy spending yielded strong revenue growth, Reuters reported.

stories.title: British AI chip startup Fractile is valued at $7 billion, with UK government backing
stories.summary: Fractile, based in London and Bristol, was valued at $7 billion in its latest funding round, which included backing from the British government, according to Reuters; it says its chips run AI models faster and on less energy.

stories.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts how DNA changes play out cell by cell
stories.summary: Trained on more than 100 million single-cell profiles across 68 tissues, AlphaGenome 2 finds nearly twice as many variants that change gene activity as DeepMind's previous best model, per the company; it is free for non-commercial research.

predictions.note: AlphaGenome 2 links DNA variants to effects in specific cell types, a research tool that could point to disease causes; no treatment yet.

stories.title: A Republican senator calls on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to step down
stories.summary: Senator Kevin Cramer of the Senate Banking Committee called on Huang to step down after the disclosure of his affair with a businesswoman US security services suspect of being a Chinese intelligence asset, an allegation China calls groundless.

stories.title: England's university regulator says students pass some assessments in minutes with AI
stories.summary: The Office for Students says students can often use AI 'in ways that cannot be reliably detected', with some assessments completed in minutes, and calls AI a 'generational risk' to universities.

stories.title: Serve Robotics opens its 2,000 sidewalk delivery robots to developers and AI agents
stories.summary: Serve's new AV Delivery Developer Portal lets third-party developers, small businesses and even autonomous AI agents book its 2,000 sidewalk robots in 150 neighborhoods, with access approved by staff. CEO Ali Kashani: 'Why does getting something delivered from China cost $1, but from Chinatown cost $10?'

stories.title: SpaceX is reportedly designing its own AI racks for data centers on Earth and in orbit
stories.summary: SpaceX is reportedly developing a 'Kessel' rack-scale system with 72 Nvidia Rubin GPUs on an 84-layer circuit board, for data centers on Earth and in orbit, according to SemiAnalysis via Tom's Hardware.

predictions.note: SpaceX is reportedly designing AI racks meant for orbital data centers as well as Earth; a reported design step, not a launch.

transcript.t: It's Thursday, November 12, and this is the Singularity Daily.
Here's your day in superintelligence, in 3 minutes flat.
Today's about proof.
A Nobel winner's team says OpenAI's AI solved half a million-dollar physics problem.
Their honest verdict? "We do not claim to fully understand the proof yet."
When Trump and Xi meet next week, America says they'll advance a new dialogue on superintelligence.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants to keep "hu man judgment firmly in command of this technology."
This week OpenAI unveiled a kill switch for its research models.
Stop time? 35 seconds, max.
Google staff are reportedly testing a fast new Gemini, code-named Hydrogen. Fitting name.
Now, the money.
Anthropic's bankers are reportedly weighing a $1.5 trillion price tag.
OpenAI reportedly hit $10 billion in quarterly revenue, and lost even more.
CoreWeave, which rents out computing power for AI, jumped over 20% and sparked a rally.
And British chip startup Fractile is now worth $7 billion, with the UK government on board.
Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts how a change in your DNA plays out, cell by cell.
It spots nearly twice as many DNA changes that affect genes, and researchers can use it for free.
The catch? A senator now wants Nvidia's boss, Jensen Huang, to quit over the spy scandal.
In England, students are passing some uni assessments in minutes, with AI.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Serve Robotics just opened its 2,000 sidewalk delivery robots to anyone, even AI agents.
Their pitch? "Why does getting something delivered from China cost $1, but from Chinatown cost $10?"
And SpaceX is reportedly designing its own AI racks, for data centers here and in orbit.
Machines can do the work now. Proving it, and understanding it, is still up to us.
Zoom out, and the line only goes up.
And the future keeps arriving ahead of schedule.
One day, all of this. Tomorrow, probably more.
You've been watching the Singularity Daily.
See you tomorrow.
Want the whole month? Hear more on November 27.
